title: What to Do When You've Been Ghosted with Jennice Vilhauer, PhD

sentences.en: Hello, and welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a bi-weekly podcast from the American Psychological
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是一档由美国心理学会

sentences.en: Association that explores the connections between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 出品的双周播客，主要探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Caitlin Luna.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人凯特琳·卢娜。

sentences.en: You've been dating this great person for a while now.
sentences.zh: 你和一个很棒的人已经约会一段时间了。

sentences.en: The hours you spend together feel like mere minutes.
sentences.zh: 你们在一起度过的时间感觉就像区区几分钟。

sentences.en: You're constantly texting, sharing photos, sending sappy kiss face emojis.
sentences.zh: 你们一直在发短信、分享照片、发送肉麻的亲吻表情符号。

sentences.en: And then suddenly, he stops answering your texts.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，他不再回复你的短信了。

sentences.en: Your calls go right to her voicemail, and they ignore your DMs. What happened?
sentences.zh: 你的电话直接转入了她的语音信箱，他们还忽略了你的私信。发生什么事了？

sentences.en: You've been ghosted.
sentences.zh: 你被“隐形”了，也就是被甩了。

sentences.en: It's a heartbreaking fact in the modern dating world.
sentences.zh: 这是现代约会世界中一个令人心碎的事实。

sentences.en: Sometimes people are left just hanging without any explanation.
sentences.zh: 有时人们会被晾在一边，没有任何解释。

sentences.en: And for those of you who've been ghosted, not only does it shatter your self-esteem, it can also hurt as much as physical pain.
sentences.zh: 对于那些被“隐形”过的人来说，这不仅会摧毁你的自尊心，其带来的痛苦甚至不亚于身体上的疼痛。

sentences.en: And to those of you out there who've done the ghosting, and I know they're out there, what's up with you?
sentences.zh: 而对于那些曾经“隐形”过别人的人——我知道这样的人确实存在——你们到底是怎么想的？

sentences.en: Okay, no shaming here.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这里不进行羞辱。

sentences.en: We're going to get to that soon with our guest today, psychologist
sentences.zh: 我们马上就会和今天的嘉宾心理学家

sentences.en: Dr. Janice Villhauer.
sentences.zh: 珍妮丝·维尔豪尔博士一起探讨这个问题。

sentences.en: She's the author of the popular Psychology Today articles, Why
sentences.zh: 她是《今日心理学》热门文章《为什么

sentences.en: Ghosting Hurts So Much, and Did the Internet Break Love?
sentences.zh: 隐形会带来如此大的痛苦》和《互联网打破了爱情吗？》的作者。

sentences.en: She's here to help us understand why people do this and what you should do if you've been ghosted.
sentences.zh: 她来到这里帮助我们理解为什么人们会这样做，以及如果你被“隐形”了应该怎么做。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Villhauer.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，维尔豪尔博士。

sentences.en: Hi, thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 嗨，非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: Same here, same here.
sentences.zh: 我也是，我也是。

sentences.en: We're happy to have you on the show discussing this very, very important topic.
sentences.zh: 我们很高兴你能来节目中讨论这个非常非常重要的话题。

sentences.en: In your article, Why Ghosting Hurts So Much, you quoted someone who said they consider themselves to be an honest and straightforward person, yet they had ghosted someone.
sentences.zh: 在你的文章《为什么隐形会带来如此大的痛苦》中，你引用了一个人的话，他们认为自己是一个诚实直率的人，然而他们却对别人进行了“隐形”。

sentences.en: So I'm curious, what would cause in a self-described honest individual to ghost?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，是什么原因会让一个自称诚实的人去“隐形”别人？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Well, I think that we all engage in a level of sort of self-justification for our behavior.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们所有人都会对自己的行为进行某种程度的自我合理化。

sentences.en: And,
sentences.zh: 而且，

sentences.en: you know, we all know why we do what we do in a way that no one else can ever know that, because we have all of our thoughts in our head and all of our kind of
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们都以一种别人永远无法得知的方式知道自己为什么要这样做，因为我们脑海中有着所有的想法，并且把

sentences.en: reasons lined up for why we make certain choices.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们会做出某种选择的所有理由都整理好了。

sentences.en: So most people in their own mind sort of believe that they're doing the thing that is best for them.
sentences.zh: 所以大多数人在他们自己的心智中会觉得自己正在做对他们来说最好的事情。

sentences.en: And oftentimes, they're not really thinking about the impact that that has on another person.
sentences.zh: 而且通常情况下，他们并没有真正考虑这对另一个人产生的影响。

sentences.en: So what inspired you to write that article for Psychology Today?
sentences.zh: 那么是什么启发你为《今日心理学》写那篇文章的呢？

sentences.en: You know, I like to write articles that I think are going to be of value to people that I work with.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我喜欢写那些我认为对跟我共事的人有价值的文章。

sentences.en: And I know that within a very short period of time, I think I wrote the article back in 2015, I had three different patients that had all been ghosted by somebody.
sentences.zh: 我知道在很短的一段时间内——我想我是在2015年写的这篇文章——我有三个不同的病人都被某人给“隐形”了。

sentences.en: And it was just really, one, kind of remarkable to see that this was becoming such a common behavior.
sentences.zh: 这真的，一方面让人觉得有点震惊，看到这种行为正变得如此普遍。

sentences.en: But two, it was very evident that it was also very, very painful and that people really didn't know how to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，很明显这也是非常非常痛苦的，而且人们真的不知道该如何应对。

sentences.en: And so I wanted to personally understand it more.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望能从个人层面更多地去理解它。

sentences.en: But also, I wanted to be able to kind of offer something to people who are going through this really difficult situation.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我也希望能为那些正在经历这个非常艰难处境的人提供一些帮助。

sentences.en: Can you explain how being ghosted can activate the same pathways in your brain as physical pain?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下为什么被“隐形”会激活大脑中与身体疼痛相同的神经通路吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以的。

sentences.en: So pain, physical pain and emotional pain are actually on the same neuropathway.
sentences.zh: 所以疼痛，身体疼痛和情感疼痛其实在同一条神经通路上。

sentences.en: And so they've done a lot of research that shows that social rejection can cause the same level of pain that sort of an injury to your body would cause.
sentences.zh: 所以他们做了很多研究表明，社交排斥会引起与身体受伤相同程度的痛苦。

sentences.en: And it's sort of activated in the same region of the brain.
sentences.zh: 并且它是在大脑的同一区域被激活的。

sentences.en: And so they've done studies that show people can take Tylenol that will actually help alleviate emotional pain.
sentences.zh: 所以他们做过研究表明，人们吃泰诺实际上可以帮助缓解情感疼痛。

sentences.en: So that's actually something that, you know, someone can do if they're really in a kind of acute state of emotional pain, that that helps a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上是你知道的，如果有人真的处于某种急性情感痛苦状态时可以做的事情，这确实有一点帮助。

sentences.en: That's fascinating that there's that connection because you wouldn't think, I mean, I would never
sentences.zh: 太神奇了，竟然有这种联系，因为你绝对不会想到，我的意思是，我绝对

sentences.en: think in a million years that Tylenol could help you feel better if you were experiencing some kind of emotional pain.
sentences.zh: 做梦也没想到如果你经历了某种情感痛苦，泰诺能帮你感觉好一点。

sentences.en: Well, I think it explains why so many times people try to numb themselves when they're feeling emotional pain.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这解释了为什么很多时候人们在感受到情感痛苦时会试图让自己麻木。

sentences.en: You know, they'll drink alcohol or take, you know, other kind of drugs or medications that
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们会喝酒或者服用，你知道的，其他种类的药物来

sentences.en: really try to help, you know, kind of just numb the actual part of the brain that's creating what feels like the emotional distress.
sentences.zh: 真正试着帮助，你知道的，仅仅麻痹大脑中那个正在制造所谓情感困扰的实际部位。

sentences.en: You spoke just a few minutes ago about how people ghost because they know in their heads why they're justifying their behaviors.
sentences.zh: 你几分钟前刚说过，人们之所以“隐形”别人，是因为他们心里知道自己为什么要将自己的行为合理化。

sentences.en: But specifically to romantic relationships, why do you think we see ghosting happen so often in the dating world?
sentences.zh: 但具体到恋爱关系，为什么你认为我们在约会世界中会如此频繁地看到“隐形”现象的发生？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's something that has always occurred throughout time, but just maybe not on the scale that it's happening now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这种事一直以来都在发生，只是可能不像现在这样规模庞大。

sentences.en: I think part of that has to do with, you know, a very big cultural shift that has happened in dating, you know, particularly the internet, I think has been one source of that,
sentences.zh: 我认为部分原因与约会中发生的非常巨大的文化转变有关，你知道，特别是互联网，我认为它是那个

sentences.en: that big shift that has been happening.
sentences.zh: 正在发生的大转变的源头之一。

sentences.en: And that doesn't mean I think that the internet is bad or somehow, you know, been a negative thing for love.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着我认为互联网是坏的，或者在某种程度上对爱情来说是一个消极的事物。

sentences.en: But I do think that it's like anything, there's good and there's bad.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为这就像任何事物一样，有好也有坏。

sentences.en: And I think one of the consequences is that people are a bit more indifferent to one another.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为其中一个后果就是人们彼此之间变得更加冷漠了。

sentences.en: And I think that it, when you meet somebody online, there's less social accountability because you're oftentimes meeting people that are not in your social circle that don't
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，当你在线上遇到某人时，社会问责度会降低，因为你通常遇到的人并不在你的社交圈子里，他们不

sentences.en: know other people.
sentences.zh: 认识其他人。

sentences.en: And it just becomes much easier to move on from a relationship very quickly when you
sentences.zh: 而当你

sentences.en: don't have anybody else in your social circle that is going to, you know, object to the way that you're treating somebody else.
sentences.zh: 社交圈里没有任何其他人会对你对待别人的方式提出异议时，想要非常迅速地从一段关系中抽身就会变得容易得多。

sentences.en: And that's what you think might be different from the paSt. Like, I mean, kind of imagining like,
sentences.zh: 而你认为这可能与过去不同。比如，我的意思是，想象一下，

sentences.en: you know, in the past, if even before cell phones, if you gave your phone number to someone,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在过去，甚至在手机出现之前，如果你把电话号码给某人，

sentences.en: you went on a few dates and it didn't work out, you could probably screen their calls or something when you had the, you know, voicemail recorder.
sentences.zh: 你们约会了几次却没成，当你有语音信箱录音机时，你可能还可以筛选他们的电话什么的。

sentences.en: So that was probably still happening, I imagine.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这种事过去可能还是在发生。

sentences.en: But as you're saying, with the internet's made people more distant, or there's just not those
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，互联网让人们变得更加疏离，或者说缺少了那些

sentences.en: mutual connections that might cause a person to under, you know, societal pressure, at least acknowledge the person and say, you know, I'm not interested.
sentences.zh: 共同的联系，这些联系可能会促使一个人在社会压力下，至少承认对方并说，你知道的，我没兴趣。

sentences.en: You know, let's move on with our lives.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，让我们各自过好自己的生活吧。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Well, I think it's a number of factors.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这是由许多因素导致的。

sentences.en: I mean, number one, there's the quantity
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，第一，我们现在能够接触到的人数

sentences.en: of people that we now have access to, right?
sentences.zh: 量巨大，对吧？

sentences.en: So it's very easy to kind of look at a page of potential dating, you know, mates and sort of see that there's just many, many, many people out there to meet.
sentences.zh: 所以浏览一页潜在的约会对象页面非常容易，并且能看到外面有非常、非常、非常多的人可以去认识。

sentences.en: And so it makes the ideal seem more possible and the pursuit of that kind of ideal relationship.
sentences.zh: 因此这让理想状态看起来更有可能实现，也让人更渴望去追求那种理想的关系。

sentences.en: And I think people have in a lot of ways developed what's called a consumerism mindset around dating, where it's kind of, you sort of believe you can shop for
sentences.zh: 而且我认为人们在很多方面围绕约会发展出了一种所谓的消费主义心态，也就是你会觉得你可以像购物一样挑选

sentences.en: somebody, you can just find the next person if the current relationship doesn't seem to kind of meet your ideal set of standards.
sentences.zh: 某个人，如果现有的关系似乎没有达到你理想的标准，你就可以直接去找下一个人。

sentences.en: And I think that people start to lose their own accountability for why a relationship might not be working.
sentences.zh: 并且我认为人们开始失去对自己为什么一段关系可能无法维系的反思和责任感。

sentences.en: They don't really realize that a relationship might not be working out because of things that they personally are doing.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有真正意识到一段关系之所以无法维系，可能是因为他们自己个人所做的事情。

sentences.en: So I think that there's different factors that play out there.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这里面起作用的是不同的因素。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that's, you talked a lot about that in your article, did the internet break love, which by the way, that title is just really spot on and very, very good.
sentences.zh: 而这，你在你的文章《互联网打破了爱情吗》中深入探讨了这一点，顺便说一句，那个标题真的非常贴切，而且非常、非常棒。

sentences.en: There's obviously some factors that are lost through the apps.
sentences.zh: 显然有些因素通过应用程序丢失了。

sentences.en: Like number one, there's the abundance of people, you know, the indifference you might see, the lack of mutual connections that connect you with other
sentences.zh: 比如第一，大量的人，你知道的，你可能会看到的冷漠，缺乏共同的联系，这些联系能将你和

sentences.en: people longer than just an initial date or something like that.
sentences.zh: 除了初次约会之类的人维持比这更长的关系。

sentences.en: But what else is lost through internet dating apps?
sentences.zh: 但通过网络约会应用程序还丢失了什么呢？

sentences.en: I mean, a lot of people are on them today.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在很多人都在使用它们。

sentences.en: I've certainly met a lot of people who have found their significant other through online dating apps.
sentences.zh: 我当然也遇到过很多通过在线约会应用程序找到另一半的人。

sentences.en: But what is missing today that might have been different in the past?
sentences.zh: 但今天到底缺少了什么，而这在过去可能有所不同呢？

sentences.en: Well, like I said, I don't think that it's all good or all bad.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就像我说的，我不认为这全都是好事或全都是坏事。

sentences.en: I think that, you know, like you said, I know lots of people who have also met their significant others.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道的，就像你说的，我也认识很多找到另一半的人。

sentences.en: So I think there is a lot of, you know, value in the ability to meet people that are outside your social circles and to have, you know, just greater access to potential partners.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为结识社交圈之外的人以及拥有更多接触潜在伴侣的机会，这里面有很多价值。

sentences.en: But I think that what happens is over time, the more sort of choice you have, the more people start to lose their own value in some way.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得发生的情况是，随着时间推移，你的选择越多，人们某种程度上越开始失去自身的价值。

sentences.en: So when you only have, you know, two or three people to choose from, there's greater value that each one of those people are going to have.
sentences.zh: 所以当你只有两三个人可供选择时，这其中每一个人都会具有更大的价值。

sentences.en: But when you've got hundreds of people to choose from, people almost in some ways lose their value,
sentences.zh: 但当你有一百个人可以挑选时，人们在某种程度上几乎失去了他们的价值，

sentences.en: because you can always find the next person if, you know, this one particular person isn't sort of satisfying or gratifying all the sort of ideals that you have for a relationship.
sentences.zh: 因为如果这个特定的人并不能满足你对恋爱关系的所有理想，你总能找到下一个人。

sentences.en: So there's a level of indifference that I think occurs.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为存在着一定程度的冷漠。

sentences.en: You know, when 100 people are emailing you, you can't possibly respond to all of those people.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当有一百个人给你发邮件时，你不可能回复所有人。

sentences.en: And you just start to develop a level of, I guess, indifference is the best word that I have to really describe that.
sentences.zh: 你开始产生某种程度的——我猜“冷漠”是用来真正形容这一现象最好的词。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: How can you fight back against that indifference?
sentences.zh: 你如何对抗这种冷漠？

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, you said you're not going to respond to those 100 messages.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很显然，你说过你不会回复那100条消息。

sentences.en: But are there tips that you might offer someone, you know, who is using online dating and away in ways to stay more engaged
sentences.zh: 但你有没有什么建议可以提供给那些使用网络约会的人，有什么方法可以让他们在这段经历中保持更多的投入

sentences.en: than the experience and have a better outcome for themselves?
sentences.zh: 并为自己带来更好的结果？

sentences.en: And, you know, hopefully they meet a mate?
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，希望他们能遇到伴侣？

sentences.en: Well, I think the problem is broader than just social dating apps.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这个问题比单纯的社交约会应用程序更广泛。

sentences.en: I think, you know, there's been a loss of, I think, sort of overall general empathy for people.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道的，人们对他人整体上普遍的同理心已经有所丢失。

sentences.en: And that's one of the things that happens, I think, as a consequence of social media in general, that, you know, there's people
sentences.zh: 我认为这是社交媒体普遍带来的后果之一，你知道的，人们

sentences.en: just feel that they can kind of speak to people any way that they want to, that they can, you know, treat people in a just much more indifferent sort of way.
sentences.zh: 只是觉得他们可以以任何他们想要的方式对别人说话，他们可以，你知道的，以一种更加冷漠的方式对待别人。

sentences.en: And so, you know, how do you counter that?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，如何反击这种现象？

sentences.en: I think you have to make a deliberate sort of intention to really want to kind of think about the other person's feelings, to really care about the other person's feelings.
sentences.zh: 我认为你必须做出深思熟虑的意图，真正去思考另一个人的感受，真正关心另一个人的感受。

sentences.en: And the reality is, you know, of the people who have been ghosted, 50% of those have actually also ghosted other people.
sentences.zh: 而现实是，你知道的，在那些被“隐形”过的人当中，有50%的人其实也对其他人做过“隐形”。

sentences.en: So I think what happens is that once you've experienced it yourself, you also become sort of indifferent to it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为发生的情况是，一旦你自己经历过它，你对它也会变得有些冷漠。

sentences.en: And people are just starting to kind of shut down emotionally around sort of how they treat others in a dating environment.
sentences.zh: 在约会环境中，人们在对待他人的态度上开始从情感上选择关闭。

sentences.en: And I think you have to really make the deliberate effort to say, I want to be kind and respectful to somebody.
sentences.zh: 我认为你必须付出刻意的努力去说：我想对某人表现得善良和尊重。

sentences.en: And, you know, it doesn't have to require a huge amount of effort.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这不需要付出巨大的努力。

sentences.en: You can send somebody even just one sentence that says, you know, hey, it was great to meet you, but I don't think that this is going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以给某人发送仅仅一句话，上面写着，你知道的，嘿，很高兴认识你，但我觉得这没什么进展。

sentences.en: I don't see this, you know, really being a connection is profoundly helpful to somebody on the other end of the
sentences.zh: 我不认为这，你知道的，真的能成为一段连结，这对处于情况另一端的

sentences.en: situation, because it allows them to understand what was going on, like what happens, right?
sentences.zh: 人有着深远的帮助，因为这能让他们明白到底发生了什么，就像是怎么回事，对吧？

sentences.en: Because when you ghost somebody, you literally have absolutely no idea what happened to them.
sentences.zh: 因为当你把某人“隐形”时，你真的完全不知道他们身上发生了什么。

sentences.en: They could be lying in a hospital bed, for all you know, you have no way of knowing how to respond.
sentences.zh: 据你所知，他们可能正躺在医院病床上，你根本无从得知该如何回应。

sentences.en: So I think that intentional effort to think about the other person and to just try to be kind and to just, you know, think about how would you want to be treated in that situation?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为那种刻意的努力去为他人着想，去努力保持善良，去，你知道的，思考一下在这种情况下你希望自己如何被对待？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's what is probably the worst part is when you don't have any explanation, you're just left hanging.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这可能最糟糕的部分就是当你没有任何解释时，你只是被晾在一边。

sentences.en: You don't know what the situation could be.
sentences.zh: 你不知道情况会是怎样。

sentences.en: Did something bad happen to the person?
sentences.zh: 这个人是发生了什么不好的事吗？

sentences.en: Did they just lose interest?
sentences.zh: 还是他们只是失去了兴趣？

sentences.en: I mean, that hurts if you don't, you're just left hanging without any explanation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你不明白，只是没有任何解释地被晾在一边，那真的很痛苦。

sentences.en: You spend a lot of time kind of ruminating on why that might happen.
sentences.zh: 你会花很多时间反刍为什么会发生这种事。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, you can't get into specifics, but your clients were going through this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，你无法深入细节，但你的客户正在经历这一切。

sentences.en: Were they, what kind of feelings were they left with when this happened to them?
sentences.zh: 当这种事发生在他们身上时，他们怀着的是什么样的心情？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So disposable, used, really terrified of having this happen to them again.
sentences.zh: 感觉自己像个用完即弃的垃圾，被利用了，非常害怕这种事会再次发生在自己身上。

sentences.en: A lot of times they'll spend hours trying to figure out what it is that they did wrong.
sentences.zh: 很多时候他们会花上几个小时试图弄清楚究竟是自己哪里做错了。

sentences.en: And so, you know, it's, it's a very, very painful experience for people to go through.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这对经历这一切的人来说是一次非常、非常痛苦的经历。

sentences.en: Oftentimes there's obviously anger and, you know, in my mind, that's actually one of the healthier responses to have is to kind of,
sentences.zh: 通常显然会有愤怒，你知道的，在我看来，这实际上是比较健康的反应之一，就是去，

sentences.en: you know, really understand that it really did not mean anything about, you know, the person who's
sentences.zh: 你知道的，真正明白这其实并不代表什么，你知道的，对于被“隐形”的人来说

sentences.en: been ghosted, but is really more of a reflection on the person who did the ghosting.
sentences.zh: 没有任何不好的含义，但这更多的是对实施“隐形”那个人的一种反映。

sentences.en: So I think anger is probably a healthier response to the situation, but oftentimes it's, it's just so
sentences.zh: 所以我认为愤怒可能是对这种状况更健康的反应，但通常情况下，这实在

sentences.en: impossible to understand how somebody could do that to them that it's just very, very devastating.
sentences.zh: 让人无法理解为什么有人会对自己做出这种事，以至于这变得非常、非常毁灭性。

sentences.en: So how do you move on from that?
sentences.zh: 那么你如何从这种状态中走出来呢？

sentences.en: I mean, what do you, what advice do you give to someone to help them move on from those feelings?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你给别人什么建议来帮助他们从这些情绪中走出来？

sentences.en: And also, is there a way to protect yourself against this from happening in the future?
sentences.zh: 还有，有没有什么方法可以保护自己免受未来再次发生这种事？

sentences.en: You know, I wish I could say that there was, I think, you know, the best way to protect yourself
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我希望我能说有，我认为，你知道的，保护自己最好的方法

sentences.en: is to, you know, really be careful about who you're choosing, you know, to, to spend time with,
sentences.zh: 就是，你知道的，真正谨慎地选择你要花时间相处的人，

sentences.en: look for those red flags kind of early on in terms of, you know, how somebody treats you from, you know, the very initial kind of contact.
sentences.zh: 从最开始的接触开始，就要在某种程度上注意观察那些关于某人如何对待你的危险信号。

sentences.en: But the truth is sometimes there just really is no way to, to know.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，有时真的没有办法知道。

sentences.en: And, you know, if it happens, you know, my advice is the first few sort of days is
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，如果真的发生了，你知道的，我的建议是头几天

sentences.en: to do nothing because the, the instinct is to kind of want to, you know, find out immediately and to contact the person over and over.
sentences.zh: 什么都不要做，因为人的本能是想要，你知道的，立刻去弄清楚并一次又一次地联系对方。

sentences.en: And that's really the worst thing to do when somebody chooses to ghost you.
sentences.zh: 而这恰恰是当有人选择对你“人间蒸发”时最不该做的事。

sentences.en: That's a very deliberate decision that they are making.
sentences.zh: 这是他们做出的一个非常深思熟虑的决定。

sentences.en: You know, nobody kind of forgets to call you back when they're dating somebody.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在跟别人约会时，没人会随随便便忘记给你回电话。

sentences.en: It's that they're choosing this behavior.
sentences.zh: 而是他们选择了这种行为。

sentences.en: They have made a decision that they want to end the relationship.
sentences.zh: 他们已经做出了想要结束这段关系的决定。

sentences.en: And whether you agree with the way that they're choosing to go about that or not, it's better for you to kind of take a step back and to kind of
sentences.zh: 不管你赞不赞同他们选择的处理方式，你最好还是退后一步，然后

sentences.en: retain your own dignity and to, to really, you know, reach out to friends and to, you know, talk to people that, you know, really care about you and support you.
sentences.zh: 保持你自己的尊严，并且，说真的，去联系朋友，去和那些真正关心你、支持你的人聊聊。

sentences.en: But it feels really, really bad to be contacting someone and to continue to just get that silent treatment.
sentences.zh: 但去联系某人却一直遭到冷遇，这种感觉真的很糟糕很糟糕。

sentences.en: It's, you know, the silent treatment is, you know, a very cruel thing to do for a specific reason is
sentences.zh: 你知道的，遭遇冷暴力，这是一种非常残酷的做法，原因很简单

sentences.en: because it has such a very negative impact on, you know, the person who's on the receiving end of that.
sentences.zh: 因为它对身处其中的那个人会产生非常负面的影响。

sentences.en: Kind of pivots to another question I had.
sentences.zh: 这就顺势引出了我的另一个问题。

sentences.en: So if you've been ghosted and you find yourself just obsessing about it and constantly being in touch with that person and they're not responding,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你被“人间蒸发”了，发现自己满脑子都在纠结这事，还不断地去联系那个不回复的人，

sentences.en: where does that become problematic?
sentences.zh: 这种情况在什么时候开始变得有问题了呢？

sentences.en: I mean, and problematic, I mean, like if they're, if you're just overdoing it and, you know, can you be turning into some kind of a stalker or something?
sentences.zh: 我是说，说到有问题，我的意思是如果你做得太过火了，你知道的，你会不会变成某种跟踪狂之类的？

sentences.en: I mean, that might be an extreme, but where can that go wrong where you just will not stop bothering someone who is clearly does not want to communicate with you?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可能有点极端，但如果你对一个明显不想和你交流的人死缠烂打、没完没了，这在哪个环节就会出问题呢？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I think it's so hard.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这真的很难。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's hard to know because you don't know what has happened to them.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我觉得很难弄清楚，因为你根本不知道他们发生了什么事。

sentences.en: Like I said before, this person could be lying in a hospital bed somewhere, you know, something tragic could have happened.
sentences.zh: 就像我刚才说的，这个人可能正躺在某个地方的医院病床上，你知道的，也许发生了什么悲剧。

sentences.en: You just don't know.
sentences.zh: 你只是无从知晓。

sentences.en: So I think you can send one or, I think one or two texts to, you know, or try to reach out to the person that,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得你可以发一条，或者我觉得可以发一两条信息去，你知道的，或者试着去联系这个人，

sentences.en: you know, maybe in a couple different ways, once or twice to see if they're okay.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，也许通过几种不同的方式，联系个一两次，看看他们是否安好。

sentences.en: I think, you know, it makes sense to want to check their social media just to see if they're posting or just that they're still alive or okay in some regard.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，去查看他们的社交媒体以确认他们是否还在发动态，或者至少在某种程度上确认他们还活着、安然无恙，这也是情理之中。

sentences.en: But after that, you know, if you don't get a response after, you know, two sort of attempts to reach them, I think at that point,
sentences.zh: 但在那之后，你知道的，如果你尝试联系了两次却依然没有收到任何回复，我觉得到了那个时候，

sentences.en: you have to kind of take a step back and, you know, really realize that this person is making a deliberate choice.
sentences.zh: 你必须退后一步，你知道的，真正清醒地认识到这个人是在做出一个深思熟虑的选择。

sentences.en: And by kind of continuing to try to contact them, you're not convincing them that somehow they made the wrong choice.
sentences.zh: 而且通过继续试图联系他们，你并不能说服他们意识到自己不知为何做出了错误的选择。

sentences.en: You know, in some ways, they're feel, they themselves, regardless of whether this kind of makes sense, they may feel that you're disrespecting them by
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，他们自己——不管这种想法合不合理——可能会觉得你这样做是对他们的不尊重，因为

sentences.en: continuing to reach out to them, that you're not respecting the choice that they're making.
sentences.zh: 你一直在联系他们，说明你没有尊重他们所做出的决定。

sentences.en: And so it's better to really just kind of pull back and kind of, again, reach out to people who,
sentences.zh: 所以，最好还是收回手，而且，再次强调，去联系那些

sentences.en: you know, care about you, your friends, your family, therapist, you know, whoever it is that can
sentences.zh: 你知道的，关心你的人，你的朋友、家人、心理治疗师，无论对方是谁，他们都能够

sentences.en: give you the comfort and support that you need while you're going through that, and to help you try to process it in the best way that you can.
sentences.zh: 在你经历这一切时给予你所需的安慰和支持，并帮你尽可能以最好的方式去消化这件事。

sentences.en: But continuing to kind of reach the person or demand that they give you some sort of answer is generally not going to be the best thing to do.
sentences.zh: 但继续去联系这个人，或者要求他们给你一个答复，通常不会是最好的做法。

sentences.en: And is there a particular type of person who tends to ghost others?
sentences.zh: 那么，有没有哪类特定的人更容易玩“人间蒸发”呢？

sentences.en: Do you have you identified some traits?
sentences.zh: 你总结出什么特征了吗？

sentences.en: Well, you know, so many people ghost at this point, there was a study that was done, you know, right around the time that I actually had written the articles.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，现在有太多人玩这一套了，当时正好做过一项研究，就在我写那些文章的前后。

sentences.en: This is a pretty old study at this point, about five years old.
sentences.zh: 现在看来这是一项相当旧的研究了，大约有五年历史了。

sentences.en: But it was saying that almost 50% of people who are kind of in the dating world have either been ghosted or done ghosting.
sentences.zh: 但它说，在处于约会世界的人当中，将近50%的人要么被“人间蒸发”过，要么就对别人干过这事。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's, it's pretty common that this is happening.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这挺常见的，这种现象一直在发生。

sentences.en: So I'm not sure there's a particular type of person, I think, you know, a lot of people who, you know, again, consider themselves to be really decent,
sentences.zh: 因此我不太确定是不是存在某种特定类型的人，我觉得，许多人，你知道的，他们再次强调自己是那种非常正派、

sentences.en: good people have perhaps ghosted somebody at some point.
sentences.zh: 很好的人，可能也在某个时刻对别人做过“人间蒸发”。

sentences.en: And oftentimes, it's just the easier thing to do.
sentences.zh: 而且通常情况下，这么做只是更轻松的选择。

sentences.en: You know, I think that it's just something that people do not when they're just not thinking about how it's going to make somebody else feel.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我觉得人们这么做，只是因为他们没有去考虑这会让别人有什么感受。

sentences.en: Are there particular warning signs at all that you might be ghosted?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么明显的征兆，预示着你可能会被对方“人间蒸发”呢？

sentences.en: Is that anything that you might look out for?
sentences.zh: 有什么值得你留意的迹象吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think if somebody, you know, has a lot of contact with you, and anytime there's like a shift
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得如果某人，你知道的，跟你有很多联系，而突然之间出现了某种转变

sentences.en: in, let's say, the general kind of pattern of how the contact in the relationship is working, right?
sentences.zh: 比方说，关系中这种联系的总体模式发生了变化，对吧？

sentences.en: So if somebody, you know, always text you first thing in the morning, and suddenly you don't
sentences.zh: 所以，如果某人，你知道的，总是大清早就给你发信息，而突然之间你有一两天

sentences.en: hear from them for, you know, a day or two, it obviously could be that there's just something
sentences.zh: 联系不上他们了，这显然有可能是因为他们的生活中

sentences.en: else going on in their life, they're busy, they've got, you know, certain, you know, other priorities
sentences.zh: 正发生着其他事情，他们很忙，你知道的，手头有一些其他需要处理的

sentences.en: that they're taking care of, it doesn't necessarily mean they're going to ghost you.
sentences.zh: 重要的事情，这并不一定意味着他们要对你“人间蒸发”。

sentences.en: But if you start to notice, you know, a change in, you know, a normal kind of pattern of behavior, you know,
sentences.zh: 但如果你开始注意到，你知道的，正常行为模式发生了变化，你知道的，

sentences.en: it doesn't hurt to just kind of check in with the person and just say, hey, you know, kind of curious
sentences.zh: 不妨去跟这个人沟通一下，就说，嘿，你知道的，我有点好奇

sentences.en: to see how things are going, you know, I've noticed, you know, it seems like there's been a shift.
sentences.zh: 想看看最近情况怎么样，你知道的，我发现好像有什么地方变了。

sentences.en: And so I think you can, you know, ask in that way, I think, you know, a lot of times people
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得你可以用这种方式来问，我觉得，很多时候那些

sentences.en: who are going to ghost you aren't necessarily going to be really honest and open about their emotions in the first place.
sentences.zh: 打算对你“人间蒸发”的人，一开始就未必会对自己真实的情绪表现得十分诚实和坦荡。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's hard to say if they're going to be really willing to tell you how they're really feeling.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，很难说他们是否真的愿意告诉你他们心里的真实感受。

sentences.en: But, you know, I think that's really the most you can do is to just kind of notice and pay attention to, you know, the patterns in the relationship.
sentences.zh: 不过，你知道的，我觉得你真正能做的最多的事情，就是去留意并关注关系中的这些模式。

sentences.en: But a lot of times there aren't going to be any warning signs.
sentences.zh: 但很多时候，根本不会有任何预警信号。

sentences.en: And I think that's one of the hardest parts.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这也是最难熬的部分之一。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And turning more toward friendships, do you also see ghosting among friends?
sentences.zh: 把话题转向友情，你在朋友之间也会看到这种“人间蒸发”的现象吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, it's funny, because when I wrote my article, I was very, in my mind,
sentences.zh: 对啊，你知道的，这挺有意思的，因为当我写那篇文章时，在我的脑海里，

sentences.en: it was very specific to dating, because I think there's something about a dating relationship where
sentences.zh: 它是非常专属于恋爱关系的，因为我觉得恋爱关系有一种特质，那就是

sentences.en: when that, that, you know, just different level of emotion that gets involved and really different amount of pain that occurs when, when the ghosting happens.
sentences.zh: 当那种不同层面的情感被卷入其中，并且当“人间蒸发”发生时，所带来的痛苦确实有着不同的程度。

sentences.en: But, you know, I think, yes, I think it happens definitely in friendships.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我觉得，是的，这种事在友情中绝对也会发生。

sentences.en: I think it's, it's a broader behavior that's about not feeling a level of comfort discussing your emotions with someone and choosing instead to just kind of disappear.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，这是一种更广泛的行为，其本质在于感觉跟某人讨论自己的情绪时不够自在，从而选择直接玩消失。

sentences.en: And, you know, I'll be honest with you, you know, after I wrote my article, I got contacted by
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，老实跟你说，我写完文章后，

sentences.en: almost 1000, I would say literally, literally thousands of people who, you know, some of them were people who had ghosted, some of them were people who, you know, had been ghosted.
sentences.zh: 几乎有上千人联系我，我可以毫不夸张地说，真的是数以千计的人，你知道的，其中有些人是玩过“人间蒸发”的人，有些人则是被“人间蒸发”过的人。

sentences.en: But a lot of the people who had done the ghosting, really felt very justified, because they, they felt the other
sentences.zh: 但许多曾经玩过“人间蒸发”的人，真的觉得自己非常有理，因为他们觉得对方

sentences.en: person wasn't going to listen to them, or the other person wasn't maybe emotionally going to be able to handle it.
sentences.zh: 根本不会听他们解释，或者对方在情感上可能根本承受不了。

sentences.en: And they didn't want to have to deal with that.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不想去应付这些麻烦。

sentences.en: So it's a really, I think, very complicated situation where there's a lot of emotions on both sides in terms of, you know, whether this is considered appropriate or not.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个，我觉得，非常复杂的情况，双方在“这到底算不算妥当”这一点上，都怀有很多情绪。

sentences.en: And I think you can't just kind of apply a blanket kind of statement across the board about what's okay, and what's not.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得你不能直接一概而论地给出一套放之四海皆准的标准，来评判什么可以、什么不可以。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, I imagine with friendships, as well as the question I just was talking about is,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我想象在友情中，正如我刚才讨论的问题一样，

sentences.en: you know, how do you know the difference between simply drifting away from someone and ghosting?
sentences.zh: 那就是，你怎么知道“仅仅是和某人渐行渐远”与“人间蒸发”之间有什么区别呢？

sentences.en: I think, I think with romantic relationships, it's, I could see that being a little different.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，我觉得对于浪漫关系而言，我可以理解那会有些不同。

sentences.en: Like, I think that's a little bit more of like a definite point.
sentences.zh: 比如，我觉得那更像是一个明确的分界点。

sentences.en: But with friends, like you said, the relationship type is different.
sentences.zh: 但对于朋友来说，就像你说的，关系类型是不一样的。

sentences.en: So perhaps with friendships, you might just simply drift away, and you might not mean to not respond to the person, but you might just feel like the friendship
sentences.zh: 所以也许在友情中，你们可能只是自然而然地渐行渐远了，你可能并不是故意不回复对方，但你可能只是觉得这段友情

sentences.en: just isn't working for you anymore.
